title: What Are Design Tokens? And Why Should You Use Them
summary: What are design tokens? Named design decisions stored as data. See a real DTCG 2025.10 token, its CSS and agent JSON output, and where the standard is now.
body_markdown:
Design tokens are named design decisions stored as data: a color, a spacing value or a font size, given a name like` color.action.destructive` and kept in one file that design tools and code both read. Change the value once and every product, platform and tool that uses the token picks it up.


That's the short answer to "what are design tokens". The rest of this page shows a real token file in the current standard format, what it turns into for a browser and for an AI coding agent, and where the standard stands on 28 October 2026.


> **Key takeaway:** a design token is a name, a value, a type and, ideally, a description of when to use it. Since October 2025 there is a stable open format for writing them, and the description is the part agents need most.


## What are design tokens, exactly?


A design token is one design decision with four parts:


- **Name:** what people and code call it, for example` color.action.destructive` .
- **Value:** the actual setting, for example` #dc2626` , or a reference to another token.
- **Type:** what kind of value it is, such as color, dimension, font family or duration.
- **Description:** when to use it, and when not to.


Tokens come in layers. A **primitive** token holds a raw value, like` color.red.600` . A **semantic** token points at a primitive and says what it's for, like` color.action.destructive` . Products should use semantic tokens, so you can change what "destructive" looks like without searching every screen for red. Our post on[scalable token architecture](https://www.supernova.io/blog/scalable-token-architecture-principles) goes deeper on the layers.


## Where did design tokens come from?


The term was coined at[Salesforce](https://www.salesforce.com/) by[Jina Anne](https://www.jina.me/) and Jon Levine. That's how the[Design Tokens Community Group put it in June 2026](https://www.w3.org/community/design-tokens/2026/06/17/thank-you-jina-and-val/) , when Jina stepped back as co-chair of the group.


The problem then is the one teams still have. One brand ships to web, iOS and Android, built by many teams, and the same blue ends up as five slightly different hex values. Tokens move the decision out of each codebase and into one shared source.


## What does a design token look like in the standard format?


This is a real token file in the format published by the[Design Tokens Community Group (DTCG)](https://www.w3.org/community/design-tokens/) . It is trimmed from the file we built with[Style Dictionary](https://styledictionary.com/) 5.7.1 on 26 October 2026. The[full walkthrough](https://www.supernova.io/blog/style-dictionary-design-tokens-agents) has the config and every output.


```text
{
"color"  :    {
"$type"  :    "color"  ,
"red"  :    {
"600"  :    {    "$value"  :    "#dc2626"    }
}  ,
"action"  :    {
"destructive"  :    {
"$value"  :    "{color.red.600}"  ,
"$description"  :    "Background of actions that delete data. Pair with a confirm step."
}
}
}
}


```


Three things to notice:


- **Keys start with` $` :**` $value` ,` $type` and` $description` are the format's reserved properties, so they can't clash with token names.
- **` $type` is inherited:** it's set once on the` color` group and applies to every token inside.
- **Aliases use curly braces:**` {color.red.600}` makes the semantic token point at the primitive, so changing the red changes every action that uses it.


## What does a design token turn into?


A token file is a source, not something a browser or app reads directly. A build tool like Style Dictionary turns it into whatever each platform needs. From the file above, our 26 October run produced this CSS:


```text
--color-red-600  :    #dc2626  ;
--color-action-destructive  :    var  (  --color-red-600  )  ;    /** Background of actions that delete data. Pair with a confirm step. */


```


And, from the same source, this entry in a JSON file built for agents to look up:


```text
{
"name"  :    "color.action.destructive"  ,
"cssVar"  :    "--color-action-destructive"  ,
"type"  :    "color"  ,
"value"  :    "#dc2626"  ,
"aliasOf"  :    "color.red.600"  ,
"description"  :    "Background of actions that delete data. Pair with a confirm step."
}


```


The two outputs carry the same decision for two different readers:


Question Answer in the CSS Answer in the agent JSON


What color is it? Follow` var(--color-red-600)` to another line` value` :` #dc2626`


Is it semantic or a primitive? Infer it from the name` aliasOf` is set, so semantic


When do I use it? Read the comment` description` field


What do I write in code? The variable name` cssVar`


The CSS is readable: a developer scanning it gets everything. The JSON is resolvable: every answer is a field, so an AI coding agent styling a Delete button gets a definite answer instead of guessing from names. Most token files today are written only for the first reader.


## Where is the design token standard in October 2026?


The DTCG published the[first stable version of its specification, 2025.10](https://www.w3.org/community/design-tokens/2025/10/28/design-tokens-specification-reaches-first-stable-version/) , on 28 October 2025. It added theming support, modern color spaces such as Display P3 and Oklch, and richer aliasing. Light and dark modes are described in a separate[resolver specification](https://github.com/design-tokens/community-group/blob/main/technical-reports/resolver/introduction.md) .


Tool support has followed. In[June 2026 the DTCG listed](https://www.w3.org/community/design-tokens/2026/06/17/thank-you-jina-and-val/)[Figma](https://www.figma.com/) ,[Penpot](https://penpot.app/) ,[Sketch](https://www.sketch.com/) ,[Tokens Studio](https://tokens.studio/) , Style Dictionary and[Terrazzo](https://terrazzo.app/) among the tools that support the spec.


What teams ship is behind that. When we opened the npm packages of 15 public design systems on 19 October 2026,[only 3 shipped DTCG token files](https://www.supernova.io/blog/dtcg-design-tokens-adoption) . The rest shipped older JSON, CSS variables or JavaScript objects. Even Style Dictionary's own[DTCG page](https://styledictionary.com/info/dtcg/) still calls 2025.10 support a work in progress.


## Why should you use design tokens?


Tokens are worth the setup when more than one place needs the same decision. Most teams hit that point early.


- **One change, everywhere:** update` color.action.destructive` once and web, iOS and Android all follow on the next build.
- **Design and code agree:** Figma variables and code read the same names. Our post on[Figma variables versus design tokens](https://www.supernova.io/blog/understanding-the-differences-between-figma-variables-and-design-tokens) explains where they differ.
- **Theming without copies:** a dark theme or a second brand is a different set of values for the same names, not a second stylesheet.
- **Agents stop guessing:** a token with a type and a description is something a coding agent can look up. A hex value in a component is something it copies.


The last point is new since we first wrote this post in 2024. Documentation is written for people to read, and it still matters. But an agent writing your UI needs decisions it can resolve, and tokens with descriptions are the cheapest place to start.


## How do you start using design tokens?


Start smaller than you think:


1. **Pick one category:** color is usually the right first one.
2. **Write primitives, then semantic tokens:** semantic names describe purpose (` action.destructive` ), not appearance (` red` ).
3. **Add a` $description` to every semantic token:** one sentence on when to use it and one on when not to.
4. **Build at least two outputs:** CSS for your app, and a resolved JSON file like the one above for tools and agents.


Our guide on[how to manage design tokens](https://www.supernova.io/blog/how-to-manage-your-design-tokens) covers naming and ownership once you have more than a handful.


## What changes next for design tokens


The format question is settled. The open question for the next year is whether your tokens carry enough meaning for something other than a person to use them correctly.
